arxiv-2201-07929.title: Estimating Egocentric 3D Human Pose in the Wild with External Weak Supervision
arxiv-2201-07929.creator: Jian Wang Lingjie Liu Weipeng Xu Kripasindhu Sarkar, Diogo Luvizon Christian Theobalt
arxiv-2201-07929.description: Abstract Egocentric 3D human pose estimation with a single fisheye camera has drawn a significant amount of attention recently. However, existing methods struggle with pose estimation from in-the-wild images, because they can only be trained on synthetic data due to the unavailability of large-scale in-the-wild egocentric datasets.

arxiv-2212-04696.creator: Pritam Chakraborty
arxiv-2212-04696.description: Abstract The non-identical particle femtoscopy is a technique that is developed to estimate the dimension of a particle-emitting medium as well as the average pair-emission asymmetry between the particles using two-particle correlation functions. The analysis of femtoscopic correlations for all possible charged combinations of pion-kaon pairs in Pb − - Pb collisions at s NN = \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}= 5.

arxiv-2306-10772.creator: Hao Liang, Guanxing Zhou, Xiaotong Tu*, Andreas Jakobsson, Xinghao Ding, Yue Huang
arxiv-2306-10772.description: Abstract Recently, many forms of audio industrial applications, such as sound monitoring and source localization, have begun exploiting smart multi-modal devices equipped with a microphone array. Regrettably, model-based methods are often difficult to employ for such devices due to their high computational complexity, as well as the difficulty of appropriately selecting the user-determined parameters.

arxiv-2311-15234.title: On the algorithmic descriptive complexity of attractors in topological dynamics Thanks: Cristóbal Rojas was partially supported by Grants ANID/FONDECYT Regular 1230469 and ANID/Basal National Center for Artificial Intelligence CENIA FB210017. Mathieu Sablik was partially supported by ANR project Dif
arxiv-2311-15234.creator: Cristóbal Rojas, Mathieu Sablik
arxiv-2311-15234.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cristóbal Rojas, Mathieu Sablik. We study the computational problem of rigorously describing the asymptotic behaviour of topological dynamical systems up to a finite but arbitrarily small pre-specified error. More precisely, we consider the limit set of a typical orbit, both as a spatial object (attractor set) and as a statistical distribution (physical measure), and prove upper bounds on the computational resources of computing descriptions of these objects with arbitrary accuracy.

arxiv-2406-00925.title: Dimers for Type D Relativistic Toda Model
arxiv-2406-00925.creator: Kimyeong Lee, and Norton Lee
arxiv-2406-00925.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kimyeong Lee, and Norton Lee. We construct dimer graphs for type D relativistic Toda models by introducing impurities into the Y 2 ​ N , 0 Y^{2N,0} square dimer graphs. By properly placing the impurities and changing the canonical variables assigned to the 1-loops on the dimer graph, we perform a "folding" of the graphs, which yields the type D relativistic Toda lattice Hamiltonian and monodromy matrix.

arxiv-2410-14635.title: GenEOL: Harnessing the Generative Power of LLMs for Training-Free Sentence Embeddings
arxiv-2410-14635.creator: Raghuveer Thirukovalluru, Bhuwan Dhingra
arxiv-2410-14635.description: Abstract Training-free embedding methods directly leverage pretrained large language models (LLMs) to embed text, bypassing the costly and complex procedure of contrastive learning. Previous training-free embedding methods have mainly focused on optimizing embedding prompts and have overlooked the benefits of utilizing the generative abilities of LLMs.

arxiv-2511-14639.title: SLAM-AGS: Slide-Label Aware Multi-Task Pretraining Using Adaptive Gradient Surgery in Computational Cytology
arxiv-2511-14639.creator: Marco Acerbis, Swarnadip Chatterjee, Christophe Avenel, Joakim Lindblad
arxiv-2511-14639.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marco Acerbis, Swarnadip Chatterjee, Christophe Avenel, Joakim Lindblad. Computational cytology faces two major challenges: i) instance-level labels are unreliable and prohibitively costly to obtain, ii) witness rates are extremely low. We propose SLAM-AGS , a S lide- L abel– A ware M ultitask pretraining framework that jointly optimizes (i) a weakly supervised similarity objective on slide-negative patches and (ii) a self-supervised contrastive objective on slide-positive patches, yielding stronger performance on downstream tasks.

arxiv-2512-01951.title: Pixel-Based Non-Linearity Correction for the WFC3 IR Detector
arxiv-2512-01951.creator: Sachindev S. Shenoy, Ky Huynh, Varun Bajaj, & Jennifer Mack
arxiv-2512-01951.description: Abstract The current non-linearity correction for the Wide Field Camera 3 Infrared (WFC3/IR) channel is based on ground-based data acquired during WFC3’s Thermal Vacuum 3 (TV3) testing campaign. In the current reference file, the correction coefficients derived for each pixel are averaged over each of the four detector quadrants.

arxiv-2512-16256.title: Phantom Menace in general Palatini f ⁡ ( R , ϕ ) f(R,\phi) theories
arxiv-2512-16256.creator: Rahul Thakur, Abhijith Ajith, Sukanta Panda, Archit Vidyarthi
arxiv-2512-16256.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rahul Thakur, Abhijith Ajith, Sukanta Panda, Archit Vidyarthi. We study general f ⁡ ( R , ϕ ) f(R,\phi) theories in Palatini formalism and attempt to constrain the behavior of ones that could support both inflationary and late-time expansion era in a unified model. In particular, we find conditions for which the theories remain consistent in weak gravity regimes as well as cosmic expansion eras in both early and late universe.

pmc-12448565.title: Factors associated with self-care behavior among heart failure patients in India: A systematic review
pmc-12448565.creator: Prima J. J. D’Souza, Mitchelle S. Lewis, Ganesh Paramasivam, Judith A. Noronha, P Kusumavathi, Tom Devasia, Linu S. George
pmc-12448565.description: Self-care is crucial for heart failure management and complements pharmacological treatments; however, various factors hinder effective self-care, adversely affecting clinical outcomes and leading to poor quality of life. This systematic review aimed to identify factors influencing self-care behaviors among heart failure patients in India.

pmc-12470676.title: Egg Allocation on Anastrepha ludens Larvae by Mass-Reared Diachasmimorpha longicaudata Females
pmc-12470676.creator: Jorge Cancino, Amanda Ayala, Erick Flores-Sarmiento, Flor de María Moreno, Lorena del Carmen Suárez, Sergio Marcelo Ovruski, Pablo Montoya
pmc-12470676.description: Simple SummaryThe parasitoid Diachasmimorpha longicaudata, native to Southeast Asia, is often used as a fruit fly biocontrol agent in augmentative release programs worldwide. This parasitoid species is currently mass-produced and released in Mexico to control fruit fly pest species such as Anastrepha ludens and A. obliqua.

pmc-12666040.title: Collaborative Working to Address Inappropriate ED Attendances by Nursing Home Residents
pmc-12666040.creator: Mary McCarthy, Patricia Sheahan
pmc-12666040.description: Background Increase in life expectancy in Ireland and social isolation has led to an increasing number of people living in residential care facilities (RCFs). Residents are frequently transferred to emergency departments (ED) for a variety of reasons. Studies found that up to 40% of these hospital admissions were deemed inappropriate.

pmc-13559059.title: Fluoride Toothpaste Market Surveillance in the Dominican Republic: Quality Gaps and Policy Implications
pmc-13559059.creator: Ninoska Abreu-Placeres, Luis Eduardo Garrido, Frank Lippert, Kim Rud Ekstrand, George Eckert, Guillermo Tamayo-Cabeza, Stefania Martignon, Esperanza Angeles Martinez-Mier
pmc-13559059.description: PurposeThe objective was to determine whether toothpastes marketed across the Dominican Republic provide fluoride levels that consistently meet internationally recommended benchmarks for caries prevention.Methods and MaterialsA total of 22 toothpaste products representing 11 brands were sampled from four of the country’s most populated provinces. Six tubes per toothpaste were analysed using standardised fluoride measurement protocols.
